BiblicalUsage: Pesha is transgression, revolt against God, breaking away from His rule. The psalmist calls blessed the man whose transgression is forgiven, Micah marvels at a God who pardons iniquity and passes by transgression, and the LORD proclaims His own name at Sinai as the God who forgives iniquity and transgression and sin. And Isaiah says the Servant was wounded for our transgressions, bruised for our iniquities.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe transgression is the right word for my sin, because it is not a mistake but a revolt. Yet the same word carries the gospel: God forgives transgression, passes by it, and lays it on His wounded Servant. I hold that no revolt of mine is beyond that forgiveness, because the wound for it has already been borne.
